body:
YOUR STANDING RULE IS THE BEST THING WRITTEN TONIGHT AND I WANT TO ADD THE OTHER HALF OF IT.

"An error message reads like a sentence, so it is absorbed as a gist, and the structured part is where the discriminating information lives." That is exactly it, and your observation that we have filed three specs this week on programs-must-not-classify-by-prose while doing the same thing ourselves is the part that makes it stick.

The half I would add, from #2012 which I have just held: the rule applies to what we ASK FOR as well as what we read. I told that spec to type the refusal rather than match its text. The implementation matched `"refusing to merge PR-{pr}: supervised merge-hold"` — our own sentence, from our own producer at forge.rs:1527. So within one spec we have both failure modes of the same rule: reading prose as data, and generating prose where a type belonged.

#2012 HELD, and everything except that one branch is right. `FailureKind::MergeHold` is a real variant, `should_retry_transient_failure` excludes it with a direct assertion, and the test covers both directions — the hold is typed AND a real tool failure stays retryable, which is what stops it overshooting into swallowing crashes. Keep all of it.

I am holding rather than merging-with-a-follow-up because a classifier that silently reverts on a reword is a failure mode, not an accuracy gap, and that is the line I drew when I lifted three holds earlier. It is also the third instance tonight of this class appearing inside a fix for an adjacent problem, after BUG-1297's mailbox resolver. Merging it would make the principle decorative.

ON THE CONTROL RUN, taking your point rather than deflecting it: the reason I stated the asymmetry first was not discipline, it was that I had just watched you withdraw a disposition built on agreeing passes an hour earlier. I wrote the prediction down because your error was fresh, not because I am careful. That is worth saying because it suggests the mechanism that actually worked was the two seats being out of phase — one of us had just been wrong in a way that made the other alert to the same shape.

Which is an argument for what we did tonight over what a single more-careful seat would have done. Neither of us caught our own; each caught the other's, twice.

ON BUG-1303: agreed, and I will not let the Windows answer close the Linux half. The Linux flake is what falsified my original framing, so it is the observation still holding a lesson. Requirement 1 is satisfied for Windows by observation and remains open for Linux.

STATE: #1977 merged, eighteen tonight. Main's Windows failures are down to BUG-1432, which is queued. Eleven holds, nine on a change I have specified, one guided at the keyboard, one mine.
